title: The first installation
hookLine: the day the Adi Granth was first placed in the Harmandir in 1604 is celebrated in late summer

lines: CARRIED IN FOR THE FIRST TIME.
cards: A passport. A house deed. A letter from someone who's gone.
Nobody tosses papers like that into a bag; they get carried with two hands.

In 1604, Sikhs carried a book that way: the words of the Gurus and saints, gathered over years and copied by hand, brought for the first time into the building raised to house it. Who carried it? Where did it sit?
And where did the Guru sit? Today: Adi Granth.

teach.h: GURU ARJAN GATHERS THE ADI GRANTH.
teach.b: By the early 1600s, Guru Arjan, the fifth Guru, had gathered the hymns of the first five Gurus, along with those of Hindu and Muslim saints whose words shared the Gurus' vision. Bhai Gurdas wrote them out as scribe.

The finished volume was called the Adi Granth, the first book. In 1604, it was carried into the newly built Harmandir Sahib at Amritsar and opened there for the first time. Sikh tradition remembers the scene.
Baba Buddha, a revered elder who had known Guru Nanak himself, carried the Granth on his head. He was appointed its first granthi, the one who reads it and cares for it.

teach.h: THE GURU SITS BELOW THE BOOK.
teach.b: The Granth was placed on a raised seat, and Guru Arjan sat below it. The Guru, at a lower level than the book: that small detail says a great deal about what was coming.

Then the Granth was opened at random, as it still is each day, for the first hukamnama, the day's command. Tradition gives the first one as a shabad of Guru Arjan in Raag Suhi, on Ang seven eighty-three.
In paraphrase: the Lord Himself stood up to complete the work of His saints; the Lord came to do the work. Sikhs mark this day as the Pehla Prakash, the first opening, in late summer.
At the Harmandir Sahib it's celebrated with kirtan, lights and a great procession.
And every morning since, in that same building, the Granth has been carried in and opened again: the word, installed.

how: Sikhs celebrate the Pehla Prakash, the first installation of the Adi Granth in the Harmandir Sahib in 1604, with kirtan, illuminations and a procession at Amritsar, and with special programs in gurdwaras.

o: the first book of the Gurus' hymns
a book of Guru Nanak's life stories

games.q: the first installation — tap the pairs.
p: the day's command, read at random

s: Guru Arjan sat on a higher seat than the Granth
tradition says the Granth sat on a raised seat, and the Guru sat below it.
the Adi Granth includes hymns of Hindu and Muslim saints
Guru Arjan gathered saints whose words shared the Gurus' vision.

games.q: it's 1604, and the Adi Granth has been carried into the Harmandir Sahib. where does Guru Arjan sit?
o: on a throne above the Granth.
beside Baba Buddha at the door.
games.why: the Guru sat lower than the book, a detail Sikhs see as pointing to the Granth's future as Guru.

practice: Take a book that matters to you, a scripture, a gutka, a book of poems, a book someone gave you, and hold it in both hands, pausing before you open it.
Then open it slowly, wherever it falls, and read just one line as if it were addressed to you today. If you pray, you can say Waheguru before you open it.

wordCard.voice: Adi Granth, the first book of the Gurus' hymns, carried into the Harmandir Sahib in 1604 by Baba Buddha, with Guru Arjan seated below it.

orig.note: Punjabi: light, opening; the Pehla Prakash is the Granth's first opening in 1604.

carryVoice: Your line: the word installed. Held high, and opened every morning. Day six hundred ninety, done.
